text: A terrible, unfinished mess of a game. Having played every edition since 2005, this is by far the worst release, to the point where I think it might be the last time I purchase an FM game and play the old ones instead

I've played hundreds of hours of this game now and while its not terrible they really are not improving the playing experience with this generation of FM. There are too many menus, too many options, its too detailed and ultimately just too slow to crunch through the interesting parts of the process; building a team, refining tactics and playing games. The trend for years seem to be to add more and more detail in an attempt to add to realism but I think the idea that a sports management game should be like a flight simulator is really really flawed. FM was far better when it understand what made it enjoyable and gave players as much of that experience as possible without all this other stuff that makes playing it feel almost like a job or a chore instead of something to truly enjoy.

I love this game, I really do. But as a long, long time Football Manager player - I see this company already heading towards the same mistakes. Unfortunately, as long as systems such as "Perfect Team" exist - that is, systems within a game that become its primary revenue driver - the rest of the game will suffer. If you have interest outside of Perfect Team, sadly, you will see very, very little development year by year in this game. Menus will remain clunky, memory leaks will never be fixed, and every other minor issue that you could initially look past will eventually wear you down and become burdensome after you see it pop up iteration after iteration. This game is fantastic on paper. The original concept is incredible. But without meaningful development, it will eventually suffer the same difficulties that Football Manager and Sports Interactive now face, and the company will suffer greatly for it. I have yet to see any meaningful development in the three years I've played and purchased OOTP, and I imagine that isn't going to change. Sorry OOTP, I want to support and believe, but I've been burned too hard from FM. Please do not follow in their footsteps. Continue to develop your awesome game. You need a dev who is passionate for the game as a whole, not just for driving revenue through PT.

An absolute cluster*uck of a UI. I knew it was going to be bad after everything I read and after trying the demo months ago but it's even worse than that. I'm absolutely amazed this was deemed a good direction by SI. Even as a "minimum viable product", this feels insulting to the fans who enabled the series to reach the heights it did. It's a slap in the face, a kick in the gonads. Incredible that Miles Jacobsen didn't get sacked on the spot for this, especially after misleading the FM community and cancelling FM25. I mean, how bad was '25 for them to come up with this? He recently said they "missed the mark" in an interview. Missed the mark? Mate, you shot and missed the entire galaxy. This is the stuff of amateurs. Absolutely baffling. Is there no one over there that dared to speak up? No one in a meeting that raised a shaky hand in the early design phase and said, "Guys, not to be dramatic, but I don't think this is it"? This just stinks on so many levels, and I have very low hopes for FM27. If FM27 doesn't knock it out of the park, this series will die. And there's more, but everything is inherently linked to the UI in FM games. Yeah, the new match graphics are nice. I'll give them that. The rest can get in the bin. [b]Update from 75+ hours in[/b]; [i]Yes, I am playing it. Everything I've said above still stands, but I just can't bring myself to go back to FM24. Blame FOMO, ADHD, the fact I dropped 50 bucks on this or whatever you like. The amount of jank and the number of clicks required just to get to certain menus is ridiculous. The omission of basic features, like match data after a match is genuinely baffling. Then there are the countless little UI bugs that constantly interrupt the experience. Example; I click on a player on the match day squad view... nothing. Click again... still nothing. Click once more... nope. The workaround? Click on a different player, open their profile, go back, and suddenly I can click on the player I wanted in the first place. That, my friends, is FM26. Thankfully, I can still create my own narratives and get invested in a save, so I'm managing to enjoy myself despite it all. But holy hell, there's an enormous amount of work to do before the next game. If this is the foundation they're building on... FM27 needs a miracle.[/i]

I play OOTP every day, but I cannot recommend this game any longer. Don't let the fact that I have tons of hours mislead you... it’s more a reflection of habit and addiction. If I didn’t get the game for free as part of the beta team, I honestly wouldn’t be buying it. Perfect Team is a financial success, but creatively, it’s the biggest misstep the franchise has made. It shifted focus and resources away from the core game. After all these years, can anyone really say the offline experience has improved dramatically? Many longtime players would argue it has regressed. I could write a 10,000-word essay on all of its issues, but here are some highlights in no particular order: - OOTP is poorly optimized for 2025. A single save file can balloon into hundreds of thousands of files, creating a massive burden for backups, syncing, and long-term storage. In short, cloud saves are just not feasible. - The in-game 3D remains frustrating. Animations are rough, results aren’t physics-based, and the follow-ball feature is disorienting. After more than a decade of development, I still stick with 2D because 3D is just not good. - Game mechanics are bloated and inaccessible. Concepts like traditional player creation modifiers, sabermetric modifiers, league totals, and league total modifiers are scattered and unintuitive, especially for new users. - Online leagues are outdated. There’s no official server support, so commissioners must know how to set up their own server or pay someone to do it. More importantly, there are no anti-cheat tools. Commissioners can view or edit ratings, and concerns about this are often brushed off. A simple player editor lock would go a long way to improve online league transparency and integrity. - Documentation and support remain major weaknesses. Bug reports frequently go unanswered, and there’s no official manual to help players understand how the game’s many systems interact. It’s trial and error, even for veterans. - The community wiki helps, but it’s often outdated or too vague. Developers have been hesitant to explain how core mechanics actually function, citing a desire to preserve mystery. In practice, this just makes the game harder to understand and harder to teach. - The game often feels unpolished at launch. While there is some internal testing, the bulk of beta testing is handled by unpaid volunteers like myself, most of whom have full-time jobs and other commitments. As a result, the testing window before release is inconsistent, and many issues simply don’t surface until after launch. Despite everything, I keep coming back to OOTP because no other game offers this level of control over a baseball organization. The depth of strategy, both on the field and in roster building, is still unmatched. Even when the mechanics frustrate and confuse me, the foundation of the game is strong enough to keep me engaged. Customization is another huge draw. Whether I want to replay a historical season, build a completely fictional universe, or run a modern league with my own twist, OOTP gives me the tools to do it. Few games offer this kind of creative freedom. I’ve also built a lot of familiarity with the game over the years. I know how to work around most of its limitations, and at this point, it feels more like a sandbox than a traditional game. Most importantly, running an online league is still fun. The stories, rivalries, and personalities that emerge from human interaction are what bring OOTP to life. The software might frustrate me, but the online league experience is what keeps me coming back.

The "small developer" (aka: Com2us, a company work hundreds of millions of dollars) wanted me to make a review for them, so I will. The only reason I have 26 is because my online leagues converted to it, unfortunately. Single player hasn't been improved since 23. This "Draft Combine"/"Improved" Dev Lab don't bring any further strategy to the game. Just some cosmetic things that probably took, like, a week to implement. OOTP is now just an IP that was sold out in order to be a pay to win shell with Perfect Team. The devs for this are lazy, egotistical, and actively censor any criticism of the game on social platforms. The only reason to buy this game is if your online league requires it or you like paying full price for a pay to win mobile game....on the PC.

You can feel the Com2us in this version. And that's not a good thing. All the effort is in Perfect Team, their cash grab slot machine. The base game is the same as ever with a few additions like the development lab, which, while fun in theory, break the entire idea of player development as handled by the organization (including setting a budget for). I would have liked to have seen maybe more detail put into the lab like having your highest ranked prospects get more time with coaches or the such as they might in real life. Pros: * Simulation aspect still seems up to snuff * Controlling a team over several years is still a fun exercise in balancing budgets with talent * Game play remains relatively unchanged from previous solid versions Cons: * Too much emphasis and dev time spent on Perfect Team and it shows * Rosters for 2025 are constantly incorrect, even in live start sometimes * Schedules for 2025 are incorrect * Still no way to copy league settings between saves thus requiring 15min+ to set up each new save file * AI minor league managers now DFA prospects if you're not watching * Minor league DFA's show up under MLB DFA screen making it needlessly busy * Mail/News now includes many things not relevant to your team or organization and even changing the filter still keeps the notifications in place making you check all the time anyway * Inclusion of additional in-game currencies for Perfect Team * Accounting and team budgets are still broken requiring constant editor changes to owner finances to make things make sense (even just for the 2025 season). And the consequences of being over budget are still ridiculous (who would actually gut their scouting department budget for the overall team being $1 over budget with a Win Now owner?) Example, the Dodgers, lavish spenders that they are, start the game "over budget," without a 6 man rotation, a gutted scouting budget, and if not on the Live Start, they mysteriously have Anthony Rendon on the IL (obviously put on the wrong LA team). This also makes the AI make stupid trade moves to get back under budget. Suggestion is if you have 23 or 24 and you don't mind not having the latest rosters, keep playing those and skip 26. If you, like me, need the latest rosters then wait for 26 to go on sale and pick it up. The original devs apparently no longer work on OOTP and you can feel the difference in the focus.

**FM26 – A step backwards** I’ve played Football Manager for years, and FM26 is honestly one of the most disappointing releases I’ve experienced. The game feels unfinished, frustrating and, in many areas, like a step backwards rather than the evolution of the series I was expecting. The new interface is unnecessarily complicated, basic tasks take more clicks than they should, and the overall experience feels less intuitive than previous versions. What bothers me most is that FM has always been about immersion and depth. Instead, FM26 often feels like I’m fighting the interface rather than managing my club. There are plenty of small annoyances that add up and make the game much less enjoyable to play. I really hope the developers take the criticism seriously and focus on fixing the fundamentals rather than adding more features. FM has an incredible foundation and a passionate community, but this release needed significantly more polish before being released. **Not recommended in its current state.** If you already own an older FM that you enjoy, I’d honestly stick with it for now.
This game cured my FM addiction. Thank you Sports Interactive!

I'm so depressed about this. I am an FM tragic. A CM2 veteran. By CM97/98 I was an absolute irredeemable addict. Y2K hadn't even clowned itself into existence by the time I was pulling all nighters scraping the dregs of the transfer market. There have been ups and downs but UNIVERSALLY evey edition has had more positives to negatives from the previous. Even the jump to 3d was surprisingly smooth, considering I had to be dragged kicking and screaming into the 2d match engine from the land of pure coloured text commentary. Unfortunately I am not kicking or screaming about this edition of FM. I am just despondent. Now It just looks like a bunch of AI generated garbage. This sounds like a cliche or even a lazy critique. I don't even know if AI was used in development, but thats how it looks and FEELS. But this is honestly just a reflection of what I am experiencing. A lazy and misguided attempt to "modernise" the formula has come across as completely avoiding whatever it was the Collyer brothers actually believed in all those years ago. The passion for the simulation has clearly abandonded whoever is in charge now. Im not angry, I am just sad. The world keeps getting worse but It would have been cool to fall back on the comfort of my degenerate FM addiction. It turns out the current focus group have decided the best place to drop the ball and spaff all over the legacy of Championship Manager is at the end of the first quarter of the 21st centure. Things being as they are, it doesn't matter if anyone hates it. The strategic decision has clearly been made do whatever the hell THIS is, and we will never get the magic back. I have no faith fm27++ will revert back to course. Perhaps if the devs made it possible to edit the UI in any meaningful way, something could be done. Unfortunately I think it is time another developer performs the coup de grâce. Let SI steer this once majestic beast into the slop vortex it seems to prefer, and create a proper FM.

I'll be honest - I'm part of the problem. I buy Madden pretty much every year (or every other year), fully aware that it barely ever changes. And usually? I still get some enjoyment out of it. It's always been a decent game to just jump into for a few chilled games of football, especially in Franchise or Superstar mode. But Madden 26 has genuinely pushed that patience to its limit. The biggest issue is stability. The game CONSTANTLY freezes, and the EA servers are an absolute mess. Disconnects happen way too often, to the point where finishing a full game in Superstar mode fells like a coin toss. There's nothing worse than investing time into a match or your career, only for it to crash or boot you out for no reason. And then there's multiplayer... which could be fun, but just isn't. It's completely overrun with microtransactions. If you dare go online, you're almost guaranteed to come up against someone with a ridiculously stacked team that you simply can't compete with unless you're willing to spend extra money. It feels heavily pay-to-win, which just kills any motivation to even try. What's frustrating is that I want to enjoy this game. The core idea is still there, and I've always liked the career modes. But between the technical issues and the monetisation, it's just not worth the hassle this time around. Easily one of the worst Maddens in recent years - and that's saying something.

I don't think ive ever seen such an egregious regression in a release. This is extremely unfortunate. I love this series. I completely get that the nature of the game itself doesn't present a lot of opportunity for major improvements year over year, and I was ok with that. I feel like you almost always got some kind of general improvements over the years. This thing is just... a mistake. The Ui changes are frankly worthy of getting fired, whoever made these decisions really just shouldn't be in a place to be making them. Edit 9/21/2025: The Perfect Team mode is so broken. You can have the very same team as Team X. Team X goes 100-62 on the season and wins the world series, while your team goes 80-82 and doesn't even get a whiff of the playoffs. The randomization engine is absolutely broken this year, probably because of the 101+ rated cards. The very same top hitter on Team X will hit .310 with 17 HR, and on your team will hit .230 with 8 HR. The very same top pitcher for Team X will throw a 3.25 ERA and for you they'll be over 5.25. A pitcher rated at 170 power can end up with a K/9 rate equivalent to a pitcher who has 100 power. I can't tell you enough how horrible this mode is now. As you can see, I've put a lot of hours into this game. The Perfect Drafts are fun to do, but the reality is everything is a dice roll. You can field the best team in perfect draft and lose in the first round. Yes, I've put a lot of hours into this, hoping I could do something in Perfect Team, but here I am with a team that is 90% of the top cards needed in the perfect league, and I'm still struggling to win a playoff series in high gold, 3 levels below perfect. Like I said, the randomization engine is so broken. I've literally considered selling off my whole team just to buy some packs, at least get some enjoyment out of it. The mode has become work, not fun, and all just for a "chance" at winning. It's so bad, but I feel like I'm committed to keep playing at this point. Ugh. ------- Regular game feels worse than ever. Simulated stats aren't really balanced right, players aren't performing at or around their talent levels even when you adjust the player variance modifier. New draftees are almost always the same kind of player over and over - lots of power and no average, lots of speed and average. The scouting system is worthless in this version, the ratings I see for non-real players doesn't tend to match their performance in the game. The game by default saves to your One Drive and filled my One Drive in 2 weeks. The only way to change it is to manually edit a config file. What? This is 2025...why not just ASK where someone wants to save games when they first run the game? The Perfect Team mode is more pay-to-play than ever. If you didn't pre-order, you're out like 4 of the best cards in the game that you can't get without spending a TON of real money to buy through the card shop. You'll never perform beyond Silver, maybe Gold level if you're a casual player who doesn't go to all the TwitchTV streams to get your free pack drops, and if you're not scamming the tournament system and the perfect draft tourneys 100% of the time. The "variant" drops of cards are just another way for someone who puts real money into the Perfect Team mode to veritably buy their way into winning tourneys. Spend more, win more, right? And don't get me started about the caustic community who are awful to "new" people on the forums and who behave so poorly that they want to screw everyone they can in the card shop and auction house. It's almost as bad as the US political climate (almost). The community has been asking for a separate Perfect Team league for people who don't want to spend money, but of course the devs won't do that because...how will they make money then if you're not dropping an additional $40 for 75 packs or one "great" card in the Card Shop? They need to revamp this game, or someone needs to actually compete with them. It's getting like Madden - same game over and over and very little new except the ratings. I get you had a winning formula 10 years ago, maybe it's time to start reworking some things to keep it fresh and actually make it better?

I've returned to Out of the Park after about 15 years. The long and the short of it is that this appears to continue to be the best baseball sim on the market. If you want to play this type of game, you pay the cost of admission. For the most part you should be greatly satisfied. However, there are numerous frustrations that while not game-breaking or experience-ruining, they'll significantly sully the experience. [Edit: Even though I highly recommend this game warts and all, I've selected "No" to call out its numerous issues.] While there's certainly a lot that's been added to the series since I played it, there's also a lot that really hasn't changed or improved much. Obviously I have no trouble paying to upgrade from the last version I purchased many years ago, but I would anticipate being frustrated to upgrade year after year. Most of the issues are interface-based. Broadly, the interface is great! It's functional, and to an extent customizable. However it does not play well with certain resolutions, and some screens/areas are just trash. A few examples: The pending free agent offers screen can't be sorted which makes it an absolutely nightmare if you're negotiating with large groups of players at once. On the depth chart screens, removing a player from the lineup also pulls them out of the depth chart. And adding a player to the depth chart as a starter automatically puts them in the first empty lineup spot. Why?? This is a nuisance when I want to build and reorganize them individually. As well, you have to be super-accurate when dragging and dropping on this screen as well as the scouting one, or else the item you've selected just disappears. Drop-down menus just aren't well organized. There are so, so many screens and reports. On one hand that's marvellous! But it takes forever to find and memorize the location of what you're looking for. Many links are duplications. Why does the Combine Scouting shortcut just take you to a partially-functioning Team Home Screen if that function is disabled? My BIGGEST GRIPE is that the game STILL lacks proper documentation. I remember the game lacking a manual way back in the day, or it would come out long after the yearly game release. These days, a manual doesn't exist. I member of the community told me documentation is now wiki-based. Well, yes, a wiki exists. But it's incomplete and some entries are outdated. As well, it appears to be maintained by the community rather than the development team. A lot of the information seems to be cobbled together from developer posts on the official forums. (But I'm not 100% certain of this.) The community is fractured between the offical forums, the subreddit, and the Discord server, as well as the few mods on Steam Workshop. Having all these avenues of contact isn't a bad thing! And I'm relieved the forum still exists, many companies opt for insufficient Discords for troubleshooting and information sharing these days. But it means you need to hunt between all of them to find what you're looking for. The best way to research a particular topic is the plug it into a search engine with "Reddit" appended to the query. But the issue here is that a lot of available information is for previous versions of the game, and while often it's still applicable, other times it's not. The official Discord is fairly busy and well populated, and the community has provided helpful answers to some of my questions. But others have gone unanswered. If there was adequate documentation for the game, I wouldn't have had to ask! And I'm not talking about asking how the under-the-hood, "fog of war"-style engine components function. I don't expect that stuff to be revealed, not in specific detail anyway. Many of those features can be disabled if you don't want to bother with them. I'm referring to core functions of the game that should be clearly explained. I made a detailed bug report on the forum that was completely ignored. On multiple occasions I submitted an offer to a free agent that exceeded their demand. They replied by declining my offer and requesting a lesser amount! Ridiculous. I also reported it on the Discord and a community member just replied to the effect of "Yeah, contract negotiations have multiple issues. It really needs to be looked at in the next version." What a brainwashed sentiment. Online leagues remain one of the best ways to experience the game in my opinion, but they're even more complex and drawn out than they used to be due to all the features that have been added on over the years. Of course, the commissioner/league admin can choose to disable many of these systems. But even a basic online league requires an extremely dedicated and knowledgeable commissioner. I find the much-maligned Perfect Team card-collecting mode to be a hollow experience. I had a lot of fun with it for a couple of weeks, and you can definitely accomplish a lot as a player who doesn't buy extra packs through pay currency. But this is mainly facilitated by farming the daily Twitch drops, five each from official and community streams. This requires three total hours of having Twitch open in your browser. Of course, you can mute the tab and don't have to actively watch or have it open in the foreground. But it feels like work. Another way to get ahead is by completing collection missions, which is just what it sounds like. Acquire the listed cards from packs or by buying them with in-game currency on the in-game auction house, which just unlocks more cards and packs. This will allow you to dominate the early leagues. However, it also means once you get to a certain level, almost everyone will be running the exact same cards. It's boring. Listing cards on the action house is also a chore, and the interface is maddening in that you get a pop-up whenever you sell a card, interrupting whatever you're doing and sometimes resetting your menu action. Infuriating! I also seem to get logged out of Perfect Team mode at least once per day, and there's no option for the password entry field not to hide your typed characters. Why?? Who's playing OOTP in a public place where passers-by are going to steal their Perfect Team login information? It's absurd. As well, while the Perfect Team leagues pit you against other players, there's absolutely no social interaction in-game. Some players list their forum or Discord handles in their profiles, so I guess you could look them up there or just chat in the general Discord channels for this mode. The draft-based tournaments are also interesting if you like draft-based CCG-style modes--many are free to enter, and you don't have to have the cards in your collection. But I tried it for a bit and I really don't see the depth. Since the simulated games add a lot of randomness (I mean, it's what the simulation engine does), it all feels like a crapshoot. A lot of people seem really into the Perfect Team mode--there's certainly a lot to do. Another component is the daily fantasy-baseball-like mode that allows you to guess the day's real-world top performers (as long as you own their cards). But after a while that too grows boring. Anyway, I'm glad this mode provides an additional revenue stream for the developers. But it really does make it feel like aspects of the main game are neglected. A lot just doesn't seem to change from version to version, and there are multiple features that are in dire need of an overhaul. Despite all this, the core of the game is largely excellent and as deep and engaging as ever. You can get lost here for hundreds if not thousands of hours. I still recommend the game. I just wish it seemed like the developers even cared about these issues. Note: My playing time is misleading, as I leave the client open all day when I'm monitoring my Perfect Team league or intermittently working on my online player league rosters. But I've still invested beyond 100 hours as of the writing of this review.

Been playing since 2017. There remains a great game in here but the lack of innovation, new features and/or new statistical data in the last 5+ years (The Perfect Team era) continues to be embarrassing. Just to name a few: launch angle, exit velocity, barrels, hard-hit rate, xSLG, XBA, etc. There is no Statcast type data whatsoever, despite these stats having been commonplace for nearly a decade in baseball. The skinning options remain poor and text size/formatting is a crap-shoot. Player profile pages have big gaps in some areas and awful spacing necessitating a scroll bar in others. The poor use of space would be less relevant if every pitcher with 4+ pitches didn't need to be scrolled to see all their data. You *still* need to restart the game completely to change the font style, meaning you need to launch the game 7 or 8 times just to see every font option available. Lastly - Perfect Team is a *ridiculous* experience. I genuinely regret buying FM26. I wanted to give it a fair chance, started a brand-new journeyman career on the latest 26.3.2 version, and several hours later discovered that the game can’t even handle a basic transfer window correctly. I’m managing in the Chinese Jia League. The game itself clearly shows the 2026 winter transfer window as 9 January–6 March. I’m inside that window, yet every domestic transfer I agree is automatically scheduled for 18 June — literally the opening day of the next transfer window. I tested multiple players. Same result every time. So my reward for spending hours setting up a huge journeyman database, scouting players, building a tactic and starting a career is discovering that an entire transfer window is effectively unusable. This would already be embarrassing for a newly released indie game. For Football Manager, a series that has been iterating on the same underlying football-management simulation for decades, it’s ridiculous. And the bugs would be easier to tolerate if FM26 actually felt like a major upgrade. It doesn’t. The new UI somehow manages to make information that was immediately accessible in FM24 harder to find. Simple things take more clicks. Recruitment feels more cumbersome. Player information is scattered around oversized panels. The new in-possession/out-of-possession tactical system sounds impressive on paper, but much of the overall experience feels like complexity added for the sake of being different rather than making the game better. FM24 wasn't perfect, but I could actually play Football Manager instead of constantly fighting the interface and wondering whether competition rules are functioning properly. That's the most frustrating thing about FM26: I desperately wanted the new generation of FM to succeed. Instead, after giving it another serious attempt, I’m going back to FM24 because the older game is simply a more enjoyable, more coherent and, crucially, more trustworthy experience. A management game lives or dies on confidence in its simulation. If I can't trust the game to know when its own transfer window is open, why should I trust anything else happening underneath? Miles Jacobson and the leadership at Sports Interactive have spent years talking up the future of Football Manager, yet FM26 feels like customers are being asked to beta-test an unfinished product. The UI is worse, basic functionality is unreliable, and now I have a fresh career effectively ruined because the game cannot understand its own transfer-window rules. This isn't some obscure graphical glitch — transfers are one of the fundamental mechanics of Football Manager. Shipping the game in this state is unacceptable.

TLDR: It's EA, costs way too much for the quality of the game, franchise is decent, Superstar is godawful, the rest of the game is fine, bugs are plentiful, but I still have fun playing. Look, it's a madden game. It costs way too freaking much for what you're getting. If you buy them every year your gonna do the same this year. BUT, if you're actually on the fence, here's the breakdown: Franchise mode is actually kinda fun. New coaching abilities are harder to understand and seemingly do even less than previous years, but the rest of the mode is decent. They removed a lot of the annoying filler things like the end of year interviews about promising position upgrades and what not. Scouting, drafts, and free agency are fun for me, and I enjoy gearing up for a new season. Playing the seasons are fun too. Good players demand way too much money on their contract years which can be infuriating, but otherwise, the money management with salary cap can be fun. Overall, franchise is a 7/10 this year for me. Superstar mode sucks so bad its actually embarrassing. Compared to CFB 26's road to glory, its buggier, less fleshed out, way less climactic, and a waste of time. Roster spots are based on coach trust, not your overall rating. There aren't position battles, so getting the #1 position spot is a boring endeavor. Getting weekly awards or MVP is honestly really stupidly anticlimactic, and winning the super bowl as a rookie (which is stupidly easy to do by the way) gets you literally nothing special. The whole game mode sucks this year, and they have to do better next year. Online/Quick Play is always serviceable, so nothing to report on there. Bugs are plentiful as always. Whether you catch the ball out of bounds and it gives you the first down anyway, or it gives you a stat in franchise mode telling you the numbers but not the actual stat, or buggy camera things, or not doing the play you picked, or a million other things, there are way too many bugs. Will they fix them? Almost definitely not. It'll be what it'll be. That all said, I mostly have fun playing this game. So I'll give it either a 3/10 or a 6/10 depending on the gamemode I play and how buggy the madden gods decide to make my game.

Two years of waiting. FM25 cancelled. “Biggest leap in series history.” New Unity engine. In/out of possession tactics. Women’s football. The hype was nuclear. What we got is the football management equivalent of turning up to a Champions League final and finding the pitch is a muddy school field with a goalpost missing and the ref is a guy who keeps freezing mid whistle. The UI is a crime. They took the perfectly functional FM24 menus, ran them through a blender, then redesigned them for a tablet owned by someone who’s never played FM. Everything that used to take one click now takes four. Information is buried like they were embarrassed of it. Half the buttons feel like they were designed by someone who hates FM. Navigating this thing is more stressful than actually managing a relegation scrap. Bugs? We got bugs. Freezing mid match. Soft locks. Misaligned text. Buttons that just… don’t work. Players doing things that would get them sectioned in real life. The match engine looks better (credit where it’s due), but the rest of the game feels like it was assembled by interns who were told “just ship it, the contractual obligations are due.” Missing features at launch, unfinished systems, and the distinct feeling that SI spent the extra year learning Unity by watching YouTube tutorials at 2x speed. Even after months of patches the core problems never went away. Support’s done now. They’re already looking at beta testing FM27 while this one limps along with half the player base still hiding in FM24 like the nuclear bunker its become. I’ve played this series for years. I’ve endured the usual annual quirks. This is the first time I’ve genuinely felt insulted by an FM release. It’s not just “a bit rough around the edges.” It’s a full price beta that somehow still has the audacity to ask for your money and your time. Save yourself. Either stick with FM24 or wait for Sports Interactive to earn your trust back. Or just go outside and touch grass. You'll get more managerial satisfaction watching kids kick a ball in the park. This is the worst one. From development and communication failures, technical and gameplay issues, loss of trust, and I didn't even talk about no International management on a World Cup year.

As a long time player of the game who as been a bit up and down on the state of the game over the past few years, I am very worried about this game's future. What used to be the most accurate sports management simulation game, is now a low performing, bug riddled mess, that strays further from realism every year. The first thing that stands out about this game is just how bad it feels to navigate the menus. The game is slow and unresponsive, and only gets worse the longer your session is. On top of that, I haven't had an OOTP game crash this much since 2015. It is actually astounding how poorly optimized this game is. The ratings and player development overhaul has generally been a very good change for the franchise, but more cracks are showing every year. A great example of this is that the "stuff" rating was flattened out to more closely mimic real life MLB, but pitching potentials were not adjusted, so every pitcher in the game has some unrealized pitching potential that will never be reached. Other than that, the franchise has pretty much gone the way of the console sports games, implementing meaningless changes just to have some new marketing words for each game. The draft combine and Trade deadline timer were a heavy part of the lead up to the release of these games, but pretty much have no actual utility. Another fun thing about OOTP, is the forum to provide feedback to the devs and engage with others who play the game, is rarely operational. It is down for several hours at a time multiple days a week. My last big critique of the game is the increase of the price over time. Years ago, OOTP was a great cheaper alternative to the console sports games, if you cared more about the actual management aspect than actual gameplay. That is no longer true, as the price of OOTP is now up to $50, almost the same price as a Triple A title. If the defining characteristic of the game is supposed to be it's accuracy as a spreadsheet sports management simulator, genuinely what is the point of choosing it over an actual Triple A studio game?

Or when I did a fantasy draft, and the game still thought that Hronek was on the Canucks years later. - Eventually, after enough seasons, you can't hire staff anymore because there's so many available that the game takes five minutes to load the list of free agents. As you can see, I've played the game more than I care to admit and enjoy it myself personally. However, it's simply not worth buying unless it goes on sale because it isn't worth the full price tag after multiple years of failing to overhaul much of anything.

I should’ve written this review when FM26 first released, but honestly, I completely forgot about the game until now. Having come back to it and thought about what I paid for it, I feel like I should finally say something. I bought Football Manager 26 with a 10% discount at launch, and I still regretted the purchase. To make matters worse, I also spent an additional £7.49 on the in-game editors. For the amount I ended up paying, the game simply wasn't worth it. FM26 feels incomplete, messy, and, in many areas, like it was released before it was ready. There are too many things that feel poorly implemented, unfinished, or like a downgrade from previous entries. Instead of feeling like the next evolution of Football Manager, it often feels like a game still trying to find its footing. I understand that this is a completely new engine for the series and that rebuilding a game as complex as Football Manager takes time. I don't expect everything to be perfect immediately, and I can appreciate that moving to a new foundation will come with problems and growing pains. But that doesn't change the fact that I paid for a finished game, and FM26 doesn't feel like one. At the end of the day, I'm not interested in paying for a game at launch and then waiting years for it to become what I feel it should have been from the beginning. Maybe the series will improve as the developers become more familiar with the new engine and continue building on it. I genuinely hope it does, especially for the people who have stuck with the series. But FM26 has been disappointing enough for me that I've decided this is where I get off. I've been a fan of Football Manager, but after this experience, I no longer have the confidence to keep spending money on future releases in the hope that things will eventually improve. I do not recommend FM26 at any price. If you're genuinely interested in getting into the Football Manager franchise, I would recommend FM24 instead. The club squads and transfers will obviously be outdated, but in my opinion, FM24 is the best Football Manager experience.

Good: Some upgrades compared to last year's version. Some TLC in regard to historical mode (updated splits, minors starting in 1901) and the development lab. Neutral: A significant amount of potential growth for players remains until their late twenties, mostly to enable the player to use the development lab to reach said potential. Players will most likely stay stuck at their current ratings when using the development engine only. Not the most realistic addition. Bad: Significant issues with AI-teams releasing viable prospects immediately after drafting them remain unsolved after months, despite patches indicating the contrary (this issue was not present in previous year's version). There is a lot to like about this game, but all the small things it does wrong add up to the game being unenjoyable and nearly unplayable. - Trading system is awful and is the most egregiously bad thing about FOF9. Teams will have 100% interest and enough draft capital to offer, yet the system doesn't allow it. They will (VERY OFTEN) give away every single available draft pick, resulting in them being awful for years while they recover (assuming they don't trade away those picks too). You are unable to actually create your own trades, you simply select a team and a draft pick/player, then hit the offer button and be given a trade. Its not at all interactable. You can't shop picks and players together, you have to choose one and see what the computer offers. Since it is AWFUL at its job, you are forced to navigate the dreadful trade UI to find a team that will actually put together a trade. It's so horrible. - Parts of the UI are unintuitive and hide important things from the player. It took me about 20 hours to discover where the All-Pro lists were despite looking through resources online. It is also very obtuse to reorder your depth chart and to navigate menus. - Your save files WILL get corrupted. Unless you are actively backing up every single save, corruption is inevitable. I have backed up multiple saves in a row just for each one of them to not work, losing hours worth of progress. You, as a player, should not be responsible for ensuring your save files don't corrupt on every single save. - Less features than FOF8. I haven't played it too much so take this with a grain of salt, but FOF9 lacks a lot of QOL features its previous title had. There are no quick options to change team names and logos as you have to manually edit the game files. There is no option to check what positions you need to draft. - FOF9 focuses too hard on the financial management portion (IMO), resulting which causes the roster management portion of the game to suffer. Players feel more like numbers and statistics than actual players. For example: 1. Occasionally, players will sharply regress and lose their potential. There is no (from what I could discern) explanation as to why this happens and doesn't get brought up at all. It rarely lines up with a major injury or age regression. If you keep them on the roster long enough they may randomly go back up to having potential. 2. Retirement is sudden and has zero warning signs (besides players just being old, at best). Players sometimes randomly retire, even if they are young, with a high overall and no major injury history. 3. Overall rarely truly matters. a 90 overall player can simulate worse than a 40 overall player. 4. Players don't request for trades if they are unhappy, they just have contract holdouts. The game doesn't make it clear if having high loyalty affects contract negotiations. 5. Drafting players in incredibly dull and uninteractive. You can't scout payers individually, you just get an estimate based off the scouting skill of your staff. This means that more often than not you end up simming until your next pick, skimming the estimates without any real thought behind it. 6. There is little feedback on how your players are progressing. The only way to check is by looking directly at their stats. It would be nice to get notified about major improvements or regression from players 7. There isn't a practice squad, so you generally are unable to strategically plan backups. Special teams are also lacking, as it boils down to a simple yes or no "is this player participating in special teams?" 8. While there is a system to show synergy/affinity between some players, it is only on offense and doesn't have a noticeable impact on simulation performance. - The simulation sy stem will sometimes do things that make zero sense. It will start your RB3 even if your RB1 is completely healthy and activated. It will start FBs at WR, NTs and CB, ect. - Players get injured far too often on the default settings. Even lowering them down to half typically results in a starting player getting a major injury every game Overall, I highly recommend you to *NOT* spend 30 bucks on this. There are far better options for American football simulation games. FOF8 is ten dollars cheaper and fully fleshed out if you want a similar game as this. Football Coach: College Dynasty is also 10 dollars cheaper with workshop support, better UI, and more QOL that FOF9 does.

I have to be honest...... while I'm on the fence about the game, the wind is somewhat blowing me toward the negative side. First off, the positives. The game is fun and it surprises me how many leagues are available at every level, even back into the early eras of baseball. I am a fan of a team that plays in the Pioneer Baseball League and they used to be an affiliate of the Cincinnati Reds, who are my MLB team. It brought back childhood memories being able to send players through the Billings Mustangs and have them be a part of that minors-to-MLB pipeline. The game is absurdly deep in my opinion. I was pleasantly surprised to see the Pioneer League and other independent leagues included in the game. As someone who is obsessed with sports statistics, this game does a good job of feeding that obsession and gives me a dopamine hit when number goes brrrrrrrr. I also like the dev lab during spring training. However, that's where the positives end. After an hour or so of playing, there is a bad memory leak that makes the game absurdly slow even on a beefy computer. The customization is not easy for people who have little technical knowledge of computers which makes team customization way too tedious, and the baked-in stadium creation tools are barebones at best. Animations are clunky which is admittedly a nitpick and not world-ending. While the game has a lot of pros and a lot of cons, I just can't recommend it to those who have played older OOTP games or those who are looking for a good baseball management / custom baseball league sim.

Madden 19 and Madden 22 weren't my favorites, but it's amazing how the game seems to get worse every installment. The amount of maintenance that this game had was crazy. It prevented me on several occasions to be able to complete the daily, weekly, or event missions to get those time-sensitive rewards. An advisor on the forums told me to follow a twitter account, MaddenNFLDirect, they said that they always posted when there was a maintenance occasion. This turned out to not be the case. There was maintenance that prevented me from playing even when this account made no mention of it. Events said they would run until a specific date, and the EA servers would remove them days before the time listed, preventing players from collecting rewards. There are events where it said you had to win 10 games for the rewards, it turned out to be 20 games and I had to find that out via the community. I won 27 of these games and still did not receive the reward. The tracking of challenges in this game is broken. You could complete a "tier" of Solo Mode: The Run, and the game sometimes just won't check it as complete or give you the rewards for it. This seems particularly noticeable after an update, of which there were many. And there's never any update that fixes any problems I've encountered. There would be twitch drops you could collect from watching streams, but they would either act super finicky and not track your progress, or there would be other occasions where if you weren't in the stream the very minute it began, you wouldn't have time to finish it because the time required was so exact with the stream length. They have more than one commentator team in the game this time, which is nice (Brandon Gaudin & Charles Davis, Mike Tirico & Greg Olsen, Kate Scott & Brock Huard). However, the Gaudin & Davis commentary is still the same that it was literal years ago. In addition, some of the names are said incorrectly. The game features Kylie Cox a.k.a. Sketch as a player, but the commentators refer to him as Cooper Kupp, which is annoying. Likewise, some of the commentators will refer to Pat Summerall as Morten Andersen. There are parts of the game where you can select which broadcast team you will receive, but for most of the game, it will be random if you have a preference. As far as the gameplay, it's pretty mediocre. Receivers that barely touch the ball before dropping it will be ruled as a catch- something that would never happen in real life. Somehow a QB with 99 at every attribute can miss a wide open pass. The opponent A.I. seems worse than in previous installments, as the QB will habitually throw it to covered receivers and not really go through a progression or get off their first read. Yet, defensive players can be in perfect position and somehow not make a play on the ball (even 99 OVR and user-controlled players). QB sneaks on short yardage scenarios are very easy to predict. Defensive players, particularly DBs, seem to take awful angles to tackle the ball carrier. Defensive players also seem to not be able to recover fumbles nearly as well as offensive players, to a comical degree. Unlike previous installments, tackling animations can be "cancelled" by another defender, which is mostly a good thing so that a runner simply won't fall forward 5 yards through multiple defenders. However, sometimes this will cause someone who is obviously being tackled successfully to be cancelled, and the offender will keep running, no matter what position they were previously in. I mainly use hit sticks and conservative tackles, but the dive tackle feels weird in this installment. The physics just aren't quite right with them. As far as punts and kickoffs, in my near 600 hours, I have never seen a ball NOT bounce well toward the endzone from where it hits the ground. In past installments, the game even had Charles Davis mentioning that the football was shaped as a "prolate spheroid", meaning the bounces can be unpredictable. This detail appears lost on Madden 26. For a simulation game, it doesn't really follow through in these regards. It's unfortunately a game that is decided by animations and, unfortunately, the animations still are nowhere near perfect. Sometimes player movement is choppy, other times players seem to teleport. This installment is the most monotonous that I have ever seen in the series. They take away solo challenges if you don't complete them by a certain time, which is diabolical. The rewards you play to get vs the CPU do not feel rewarding at all. The teams are always 83 overall, and extremely easy. It's more grindy than anything. There is no sense of satisfaction from these games, which are on repeat. The exception were the few events that were polar opposite of this, they were almost impossible to complete because the teams were so good...but there weren't that many of these challenging ones. Speaking of impossible to complete, the game has crashing issues all the time. A crash results in an instant loss if you are in the middle of an event game. And if you get 1 loss on these events, you have to start from the beginning all over again. These crashes were not because of low specs. I have top of line equipment. In rare cases, the game stops recognizing the ability to pick a play. You can still go up and down, pause the game, and control your players on the field, but when you press a play it simply won't compute. The games menu, particularly navigating your item binder or the collection of sets, is still as bad as ever. Some of the card packs are still labelled as "Madden 25" which is obviously an oversight. It is slow as can be and is filled with several bugs and errors. In many cases, these errors will kick you from Ultimate Team and the EA servers entirely. In worse cases, you'll be locked out of accessing your collection for some time after. In rare occasions, you'll be unable to purchase items from the store with your in-game currency, which again, prevents you from completing your daily (and thus weekly) objectives for rewards. There is not a single instance where even with mountains of proof EA stepped in to provide assistance. Trying to communicate with them for anything is a monumental waste of time. Even after making it through the virtual A.I. and being connected to several agents, the responses were still unhelpful and began with generic templates that even said stuff like "Copilot said: ". Not only would I not recommend this particular installment, I have officially been turned off from playing, let alone buying, any EA game for the future.

FM26 is by FAR the most disappointing FM title to have ever been released. All core mechanics and concept have either been made worse or completely destroyed, the UI and panels that will be what you spend the most time one are objectively terrible and the upside is nowhere to be seen. An engine change and one extra year in development for what? If you remove every single problem, issue and bug that FM26 has introduced it would still be a disappointing release. Pros: - In/Out of possession is a great idea, a smart and intuitive way to add tactical depth. - The new icons and visuals for teh tactic screen look good and fresh. Cons: Bugs Noticed (For now): - The amazing feature of crashing 1/3 times after a match finishes. IMPORTANT: If you are having this issue make sure whenever you are making tactic changes and especially subs do NOT use the undo button. This has caused most of my crashes. - Players beign dissapointed by not fulfilling pormises that you never made and the lovely fact that the only workaround is by using the paid in-game editor. UI/UX: - UI is terrible and unintuitive, things are placed all over the place, hard to find what you are looking for. - UX is even worse with key panels being 5-7 clicks away. On most panels that it takes you 5- 7 clicks to get there one back button will take you back around 4 clicks for no reason. Panels get stuck all the time during a match and you have to find what panel you need to navigate to and what options you need to press to finally get it unstuck almost as if you are defusing a bomb. - Managing, hiring, firing or doing anything related to stuff has just been made 3 times harder and 2 times less intuitive for no reason at all. - The messages screen has somehow become 10x worse. 9/10 messages you receive will be bloat/slop that is not relevant or useful, you get a lot mroe messages than you used to on previous versions. - Interacting with players or staff is a nightmare. The "Actions" button usually hides about 50 different options withotu any categorization and 99% of said options don't have any visual aid. Most used options (e.g. contracts, trainings/form praise/criticism, individual training) should have a visual cue or icon. - The competitions screen is a mess. Good luck trying to find the competition you are looking for and if you do, good luck finding the information you need. - Finances, even the most basic of information is burried tens of clicks away and navigating to it is a complete guessing game. Note: For a game that is 95% panels/UI I cannot believe what a massacre FM26 has been. It's as if they have no UI/UX Specialist working with them. Training: - Managing training is horrible. You can't copy paste sessions, picking what training you want to do is exactly the same but it was made visually worse and harder to use. You have to change every training one by one unlike previous versions where you could day by day. - Out of possession training never works. - Players are almost always complaining about their individual training. - If you want to change a player's individual training you'll have to first change it to none and THEN after passing some days change it to the different target otherwise they will keep nagging you about how their individual training is not beneficial. - Descriptions from individual training have been removed for some reason. - Individual in/out of possession position training, In possession pos has a list of all standard positions and then all roles for the selected position. Out of possession is split into "Defenders/Midfielders/Attackers" and each category has a dozen different roles. Why are these actions any different at all? Match Preparation/Tactics: - No quick subs. - Trying to swap a player on the combined view doesn't show the visual colors that represent how comfortable they are at said position. - That visual cue exists in the In/Out of possessions view BUT making changes on either will not affect the other so you will have to manually change the players on both views. - Sometimes if you make a change in the In/Out of possession views the player you subbed/swappped will be on a different side. For example you have 2 MCs you make a sub of the MC on the right side In possession, the newly added player will be on the left side when out of possession for some reason. - Quick tactic change uses horizontal arrows "< >" but if you open the detailed view of said tactic the appear vertical and have completely different icons while most don't have any icons at all. There is no consistency between menus that serve the same purpuse. - Some option are hidden behind the detailed view and can't be accessed using the left/right buttons. - When using the "< >" buttons, their hitbox is very small and if you miss it opens up the detailed display that you have to close out of. Match Engine: - Crowd audio will stop after 30 minutes of a match and will only come back if you restart the game only to stop playing again on the next. - Marking is broken. More prominent for player marking tactics that will become zonal out of nowhere for some time before reverting. - The AI is the same old, just as stupid as it's always been, simulation is not more accurate or more realistic. - Visually, player models are hard to distinguish in-match, the ball feels like a bouncy ball, visual clarity is not great especially when it's raining. - Shots hitting the woodwork. From controlled testing of 100 matches I found out an average of 2,84 woodworks against you but an average of 0,19 woodowrks for you. - Corners. When you are the stronger team, you will have most shots on target ending up in a corner and if you watch the highlghts you will see the most unlikely saves/stops you have ever seen. If the match engine decides a shot will end up as a corner don't make it a miracle save every time. - Player condition constantly bugs out going up and down so at a quick glance you have no idea how your team is doing. - Player feelings show only the face now and not the description so you have to hover over them if you want to see details. - Pressing Undo on a sub does undo the change but the In/Out icon still appears and will usually crash the game when the match ends. Youth: - Youth training is hidden away and so hard to find that a lot of people still think it's completely removed. - (Observation)Potential ability for players U18 seems off. Previous versions would get within 1 star. In this one even with 20 ability staff on average they are 2-3 stars off. Since I've only noticed this in youngsters this might be a design choice? Adult players have the regular discrepancy as seen in previous games. Conclusion: My disappointment is immeasurable and my FM experience is ruined. They have done so much damage to the game that they'll probably need to delay the next FM another year just to get on par with FM24 and that's a very sad thing I have to type out. Even if FM26 was a one-time free product it would still be the most disappointing FM version ever released.

Thank you, Sports Interactive. I started with Championship Manager 01/02 and I have played every game you have made since. Hundreds of hours, every year, for more than two decades. Before I get to this one, I want to go through them properly. Championship Manager 01/02 The one that hooked me. Attribute masking, the new transfer rules, a database that felt like the whole football world lived inside it. I still know people who fire it up now. Championship Manager 4 You gave us the 2D match engine. People argued about it at the time. I just sat there watching little dots move and realised I was never going to stop. Championship Manager 03/04 The last one under the old name. You cleaned up what 4 got wrong, made training readable, improved the media and player relationships, and sent us off with a game that still felt like home. Football Manager 2005 The rebirth. Same soul, new name. Job centre, mind games, better loans, pre- and post-match detail. You didn’t just continue the series. You saved it. Football Manager 2006 Team talks. Small thing on paper. Completely changed how a dressing room felt. Football Manager 2007 Proper scouting at last. Affiliate clubs, richer player interaction, friendlies that actually meant something. The world got bigger. Football Manager 2008 Transfer centre, FaceGen newgens, a finance system that finally made sense, board and fan confidence that could actually bite. The game started feeling like a job. Football Manager 2009 The first 3D match engine. It was rough. It was also the moment matches stopped being a spreadsheet and started being a match. Football Manager 2010 You kept polishing the 3D and made the whole thing feel more connected. Another year I didn’t get my evenings back. Football Manager 2011 Agents, more depth in deals, another step toward the game pretending it was real life. Football Manager 2012 A huge pile of features and a match engine that finally started to look like the one we still talk about. This was peak “just one more season”. Football Manager 2013 Director of Football, Classic Mode, team dynamics. You let some of us play faster and some of us play deeper. Both camps were happy. Football Manager 2014 Cloud saves, Linux, another thousand little things. The game became something you could live inside. Football Manager 2015 Happiness and dynamics that actually mattered. Squads felt like groups of people instead of lists of numbers. Football Manager 2016 Create-a-Club. For a lot of us that was the year we stopped managing someone else’s club and started building our own. Football Manager 2017 Scouting packages, better recruitment tools, another layer of “I should really go to bed”. Football Manager 2018 Press and media that felt less like a chore and more like part of the job. Football Manager 2019 Licensed Bundesliga and a match engine that kept improving. The German save finally looked like the German save. Football Manager 2020 Development Centre. Youth football stopped being an afterthought. Football Manager 2021 Expected goals, the Data Hub. You started giving us the same numbers the real coaches were using. Football Manager 2022 Game Pass brought a new wave of people in. Positional play started to show itself. The tent got bigger. Football Manager 2023 UEFA competitions properly licensed. Hearing the Champions League music in FM still hits. You also started the work that let us carry saves forward. Football Manager 2024 Save transfer from 23, a proper set-piece overhaul, intermediaries, Real World and Your World. Twenty years of Football Manager and it still felt like you were adding things that mattered. And then Football Manager 26. Unity. Women’s football. In and out of possession tactics. FIFA licences. On paper it should have been the biggest leap in the series. Instead it is a hollow rebuild. Features that had been in the game for years were stripped out. The interface fights you. The menus look modern and feel unfinished. Matches look better and somehow mean less. The little rhythms that made FM feel like your club — the inbox, the shouts, the familiar screens, the sense that the world was ticking over even when you weren’t looking — are gone or broken. What is left is a prettier shell with the soul missing. I have given this series hundreds of hours a year since I was a teenager. I never thought anything would make me stop. Thank you for twenty-five years of fun. And thank you for making a game bad enough to finally end my addiction.

FM26 managed to waste several hours of my time through a bug in one of the most basic functions of the pre-game editor. I created a custom club, a full squad of players, and an extensive coaching staff. Because the editor includes a Duplicate function, I sensibly used it to create players and staff from templates rather than entering every field from scratch. The editor displayed the correct data: players with fixed 200 Potential Ability, Current Ability set close to the editor’s own Recommended Current Ability, and the attributes and staff ratings I had deliberately assigned. When I started a new game, much of that data had been corrupted. Players assigned 200 PA appeared with substantially lower and apparently arbitrary potential. Some Current Ability ratings were raised far beyond what I entered; others were reduced. Staff data was similarly unreliable. This is not user error or ordinary CA reconciliation. The game simply does not faithfully import records created with a function the editor expressly provides. The apparent solution is to delete the affected people and manually recreate every player and coach without using Duplicate. That would require several more hours merely to reconstruct work I already completed correctly. I am not doing that. A database editor that cannot reliably copy and save a database record is not fit for purpose. This would be irritating in any edition. It is indefensible in a game that skipped an annual release, canceled FM25, and supposedly used the additional development time to rebuild the series properly. Instead, established functionality has been removed, degraded, or shipped broken. Meanwhile, Sports Interactive devoted substantial resources to adding women’s football—a feature for which it has produced no public evidence of meaningful customer demand—and then implemented it in the most intrusive way possible. Men’s and women’s leagues are bundled together during game setup. Adding a men’s league automatically adds the corresponding women’s league, while attempting to remove the women’s league can remove the men’s league as well. Users are not even given a straightforward independent choice about which competitions to load. The objection is not that women’s football exists. The objection is that SI prioritized a large optional expansion of unproven commercial value, forced it into the setup structure, and simultaneously failed to preserve basic functionality that existing customers actually use. FM26 is a textbook example of disastrous product management: broaden the scope, remove user choice, break mature features, and release the resulting mess as an upgrade. I lost hours of work because the editor cannot perform a basic copying operation reliably. That alone is enough to make the game impossible to recommend.

[h1]THE LAST GAME I HAD BOUGHT IN THE SERIES WAS OOTP 24. THIS GAME SHOWS LITTLE TO NO IMPROVEMENT OVER THAT GAME.[/h1] Let me make one thing clear: I love OOTP and I love the formula. I will likely continue to play this version of the game as I've already bought it, however: The three main differences from this game and OOTP 24 is the development lab, the development focuses, and the draft overhaul. The development focuses seem like a gimmick that barely even change anything from season to season. At best you'll be able to get +5 on that pitcher's changeup by the end of his sixth year at the cost of -5 to all his other pitches. A very irrelevant feature in my eyes. The development lab is an interesting idea, if done correctly. As I had feared, OOTP has made the normal development of players more of a chore in favor of the new development lab. I have had multiple starting pitchers with 60-70 potential stuck on 40/45 overall for multiple seasons despite also hard focusing them in the development lab. (Yes I know I can turn up development speed) The issue arises in that they've fixed development from Rk to AA, but AA and above it is near impossible to push most pitchers to near their potential, and players at AA or above rarely develop from just playing games anymore. (If you turn up development speed, EVERYONE develops faster at all levels and that's not what I want) It's a novel concept with subpar execution that can also have big impacts on your save, forcing you to micromanage it. The draft overhaul is really more of a UI change than anything. The draft combine and MLB draft leagues don't really impact much. Also had a weird potential bug in that there were no high schoolers in the 2026 draft pool beyond round 5 despite the draft percent targets being standard in the settings. The formula of the game is still the same as it's been and it is still a fun experience, but the game has been pretty much stagnant since OOTP 21. I wish OOTP Developments would get into simulating the new age statcast batted ball, spin rate, and pitch mix type stuff. That would be cool. I do not recommend anyone with OOTP 23 or later to buy this year's game. I do recommend anyone new to OOTP or someone with an older game than 23 to buy this one.

I recently got back into Madden with Madden 26, specifically playing MUT, and I really wanted to enjoy it. I’ve played Madden in the past and was genuinely excited to jump back in this year. Unfortunately, the experience has been extremely frustrating because of how poor the servers and overall performance have been. The biggest issue is the MUT servers. A lot of the time, I can barely even load into the mode, and when I do, it takes forever just to navigate menus. There are constant delays, lag, and moments where the game feels like it’s about to freeze or disconnect entirely. Trying to start a game can take way longer than it should, and sometimes it doesn’t even work at all. For a mode that relies so heavily on online connectivity, this really shouldn’t be happening. On top of that, the menus and general UI feel incredibly slow and unresponsive. Simple actions like opening packs, adjusting lineups, or browsing the auction house feel like they take twice as long as they should. It completely kills the flow of the game and makes what should be a fun experience feel like a chore. Gameplay itself can actually be enjoyable when everything is working properly. There are moments where the game feels smooth and fun, and it reminds me why I wanted to come back in the first place. But those moments are overshadowed by the constant technical issues. It’s hard to stay engaged when you’re dealing with lag, slow menus, and server problems every time you try to play. What’s most disappointing is that this isn’t a small issue—it’s something that seriously affects the core experience. I was genuinely looking forward to continuing with the series and even getting Madden 27, but based on how Madden 26 has been performing, I’m honestly reconsidering playing Madden at all going forward. EA really needs to address these server and performance problems. Improving server stability, speeding up menus, and optimizing the overall responsiveness of the game would go a long way. Players shouldn’t have to fight the game just to load in and play. At the end of the day, Madden 26 had the potential to be a great experience, and there are still glimpses of that when everything works. But right now, the technical issues make it hard to recommend. I hope EA takes this feedback seriously and makes the necessary improvements, because the player base deserves a much smoother and more reliable experience.

Not Recommended — MLS is effectively broken by a known salary-cap bug I bought FM26 specifically in part because I wanted to manage in MLS, and unfortunately the current implementation has a game-breaking issue with salary-cap calculations during contract negotiations. In my FC Cincinnati save, the game correctly shows the club’s actual salary-cap position and available GAM in the roster/registration screens. However, when negotiating a new contract, the Budget Adjustments screen displays obviously incorrect salary-cap figures and fails to recognize the club’s available GAM/TAM. Because those incorrect figures feed into the contract validator, the game can disable “Suggest Terms” and prevent you from signing a player even when the deal should be legal under MLS rules. I was able to reproduce this very clearly with Luca Orellano. The game recognized more than $2 million in available GAM elsewhere, but the contract negotiation screen showed effectively none and would not allow the allocation money to be applied. The result was that a legitimate transfer could not be completed. More concerning, this appears to be a known issue that has already been reported on Sports Interactive’s own bug tracker and has still not been properly resolved. MLS roster rules are complicated, but that makes it even more important that the game’s cap and allocation-money systems work reliably. There is a lot I like about FM26, and I would be happy to change this review if the MLS contract/salary-cap system is fixed. But at the moment I cannot recommend the game to anyone who specifically wants to manage in MLS.

Poorly implemented UI changes versus prior versions. UI scaling constantly fails to adapt to opening new windows, text often overruns or is turned into some nonsense abbreviation. Some pages still do not load entirely, despite dozens of patches. Bugs are moderately common and sometimes are game-breaking, there are also frequent save corruption issues and stability issues. I have experienced crashes on Windows + on linux on steamdeck, often without any error code or even a hint as to what could have caused it. Graphics are truly laughable at times for a game in this day and age, I never expect them to be as high fidelity as a game like EAFC, since that would be overkill, but they are easily beaten out by years-old mobile games. The lighting system is also seemingly nonsense and makes it frequently difficult to see players or the ball when playing at different stadiums, meaning you have to constantly adjust brightness and contrast on your display every time you play a new game. The tactical changes and in particular the in/out of possession changes are welcome, but they feel stifled and underdeveloped. Some tactical changes and settings do not seem to have any measurable or detectable impact on gameplay or outcomes, leaving them feeling pointless to even look at and a waste of screen space. Charging an additional $9 USD for the in-game editor also feels slimy, because the developers of course know this is the only way to fix some issues, edit things to be more realistic that were poorly implemented, or recover from bugs that would otherwise interrupt your progress. Overall, truly a 5/10 at best, and that is being very generous. Previous FM titles, though still flawed in many ways, are far more enjoyable and have much broader mod support as well, if you already own FM 24 or earlier games, there is almost no reason I can imagine to purchase this game.

This edition also feels painfully average — nothing in the game makes you go “WOW.” OOTP 26 flaunts a flashy interface and multiple game modes… but it’s all just a façade. Can you enjoy FM26? Absolutely. But unfortunately, I find myself enjoying it in spite of many of its changes and flaws, rather than because of them. The match engine is better than the FM24 generation — although I'd argue only incrementally — and it still produces plenty of moments where you look at an action and think “why the hell did that happen?” because what you're seeing doesn't seem to logically follow from your tactical setup, player roles or instructions. But that's not really my biggest frustration with Football Manager. The issues that have plagued the series for the last decade or more are still there: player interactions that lack nuance, playing-time expectations that don't reflect how real squads are managed, board reactions that fail to understand context, repetitive and increasingly immersion-breaking responses, and a general tendency for the game to evaluate events against arbitrary thresholds rather than understanding what is actually happening in the wider context of your season. In fact, I think FM26 has actually regressed in one of Football Manager's most important qualities: immersion and its feeling of being a believable football world. Some of that is undoubtedly down to the new UI, which often hides context rather than presenting it clearly, but the deeper problem is much more fundamental. Win a competition you're expected to win and the board essentially treats it like another Tuesday. Rotate your squad because you're playing three games in seven days, get knocked out of a cup you were supposedly expected to reach the quarter-finals of, and suddenly the board is unhappy. Give a player the playing time you agreed to and he'll still complain because the game appears to care more about starts than actual minutes or the circumstances behind them. These aren't necessarily bugs — they're symptoms of a simulation that doesn't understand CONTEXT. Until SI tackles that fundamental problem, I have very little confidence that FM27 will meaningfully address the things that have been frustrating players for years. Football Manager doesn't need more isolated features or more data; it needs to understand what that data means. Give me a game that understands the story of my season, my squad, my decisions and my circumstances — rather than one that simply checks whether individual conditions have been met. That's what would make FM feel like football management again.
