I am writing this review after pouring my heart, soul, and literal weeks of real-time life into a 23-year-long save. As a veteran of this series, I understand that variance, bad luck, and tactical mistakes happen in football. However, what I experienced in Football Manager 2026 crosses the line from "realistic challenge" to a completely broken, scripted, and infuriating simulation.Over a 23-year career, my team was elite. We dominated domestically, built world-class squads, and tactically outclassed our opponents on paper. Yet, during this period, I suffered around 15 agonizing exits from European competitions under the exact same ridiculous, repetitive circumstances. This was not happening with only one tactic so that is not really a viable explanation. I took over Partizan, even won CL 2 times and this is more then i would have hoped when i started the carrer. However constant ridicilous European exits have completelly ruined the experience of the save as i was constantly going out while doubling my opponent shoots, shoots on target xG and usually had a better possesion as well, as mostly i was playing with possesion based systems. FM 26 is one of the worst footaball simulation engines that i ever experienced and probably dead worst. Only reason i was playing this long is cause i want to finish the career i started and invested so much time in and becouse of nation building aspect of it. But for any new players i reccomend waiting for FM 27 and waiting for reviews before investing money and time in the game as it is currently not worth it all. I do think the game has a very good petential becouse details in the game are quite good, but noone of it really matters if u constantly getting a feedback by watching the games and stats that your team is doing well, but result in Europe quite often goes the other way. In this 23 year period i only experienced 1 tie where i was statistically worst and by watching the game u could say that too where i actually advanced. So this cannot be really explained by varience. Cause bad varience won't ever hit u 15 out of 16 times. What could be the reason is that FM is deliberatly trying to keep the traditional top teams relevant and gives them better treatmeant by game engine compare to a team like Partizan, this is not a fact thou, i cannot confirm this but i think it is verry possible after coaching Partizan for 19 seasons of my 23 year career (4 years i was coaching a national team to take a break ftom the nonsence i experienced). If this is the reasom, then obviously engine is biased and broken, therefore not worth playing. The main reason i suspect this cause i was following the results of other Serbian clubs and saw simular pattern just not to the extent i ecperienced in my Partizan. Sponsorships and reputation are very static and no matter how much deep runs u make in CL u will stay on national behind teams u trash 6-0 when u face them wich requires an editor so u can mannualy fix it and make it realistic. So i would not reccoment spending any time and money on this game unless FM 27 address this issues in Nation building saves with lower tier teams. I also played an Arsenal save for a season and a half where i watched every single game from start to finish. In Europe i never experienced this and was doing very well, reaching final in first season and was on top on league phase in second season before i stopped. Reason i stopped that save is ridicioulous home away varience where at home i won 18 out of 19 PL games, while away i couldn't win the game to save my life wich made every game predictable and i basically could guss the outcome before the start 90 percent of the time. I played a save with Serbia for 6 years and it was okayish, expect that i had no normal regens only 2 star players at best with 2.5 potential wich made me stop cause i didn't see any persepctive in the save. Overall verdict 2/5 at best only becouse of nice details, dinamic coefficients and pretty good recruitment system. Actuall game engine is just terrible and not worth paying for. Hopefully this helps. EDIT I deleted the game after a season or two after writing the review due to the ridicilous semi final against Leverkusen where i outplayed them completely in 2 legs got 2 draws and lost on penaltyes that i didn't even take. There was a bug where my team started with a missed penalty before the shoutout even began. Game is reallt not worth paying or investing any time in it.

I’ve been playing Football Manager for almost a decade, and it’s been one of my favorite gaming franchises during that time. After waiting so long for the next release and then seeing the overwhelmingly negative feedback, I was genuinely disappointed. As a long-time fan, it was hard not to feel let down. That said, I still believe the new engine and the direction of the game have a lot of potential for the future. I’m hopeful that FM27 will build on this foundation and deliver the experience many fans are looking for. Unfortunately, this release feels like a step backwards in several areas. In my opinion, the game has been simplified too much in an attempt to appeal to a wider audience and to support multiple platforms. While attracting new players is important, it shouldn’t come at the expense of the depth and detail that made Football Manager so special in the first place. I sincerely hope the developers listen to community feedback and make meaningful improvements going forward. Otherwise, there is a real risk of losing the passion and loyalty of many long-time fans, something we’ve already seen happen with several other beloved gaming franchises in recent years.

Catchers are inconsistent in throwing out runners, wild pitches are common, with pick-off attempts almost never succeeding. Additionally, foul pop-ups nearly always result in outs unless they drift foul down the line near the foul pole. My biggest frustration is the lack of administrative support in online play. Despite multiple attempts to contact them through various channels, I've received no response, leading me to question their commitment to all players. TLDR - Just go play MLB The Show for a more accurate baseball experience.

Oh boy there's so much to break down about how frustrating it is to see this be priced at $70, and for them to not even have an OUNCE of standards to back up the price. So first of all, I will say the game is playable. I've dumped a lot of hours into it, just because at the very least (even for it being one of the only high quality options for this market) it runs, one of the better pc versions, because I have no where near high quality specs, but I don't get much performance issues. BUT, it does not justify for the absolute lack of care and standards put on this game. For how many reoccurring bugs, which let me make clear, have been in the game since its release, is an absolutely embarrassing look for this company. These bugs range anywhere from player cpu performance glitches/inconsistencies, the basic systems in the game (like coach abilities, stat counting, etc.) that have plenty of bugs that are ALWAYS there and never change, and even smaller things like visual display bugs. To start with player cpu inconsistencies, there are common glitches (which appear more often in cpu vs cpu as well) that are consistently in every match you play, and very often, cause results to differ due to them negatively impacting what happens on the field. Most common one that is absolutely annoying, is lack of reaction from the defense. Linebackers will sometimes sit in foot chopping stance, not moving or reacting to a running back/quarterback running right past them. Linebackers/secondary players will very consistently watch a ball pass right next to them, and are completely unfazed about it and would rather stare at the backfield. Defenders engaged in blocks would rather be more focused on sucking themselves into a block, rather than attempting to tackle the running back that passes by a millimeter next to them, and/or defenders will literally brush themselves up against a ballcarrier without attempting at all for a tackle. A VERY costly glitch is one where for some odd reason (mostly involving cornerbacks) two players will have coverage priorities that are across the field from each other, meaning it most likely gave them the wrong coverage priority for that player, which will allow for the easiest touchdown of an offense's life. So yeah, overall, the cpu glitches are VERY defensive heavy, and will cost you negative results in EVERY game, not just some. Which in return, makes the offense extremely overpowered, even with slider adjustments. As for basic system glitches, it is absolutely ridiculous that these glitches even exist in the first place, considering how most companies would treat these as a simple patch done within a week. Starting with coach abilities, it is an absolute cluster **** of a system. Starting with some of the more infamous bugs of this system, which a couple of them come from the scouting abilities. There is this specific ability called "talent evaluator" which is a very nice ability to the game, and would be one of the most used abilities in the scouting category. Well, it is actually the one no one ever uses, because instead of doing what it's supposed to do (boost to the talent range percentage in scouting), it instead glitches your entire talent range progress for every draft prospect for the rest of that season, making it impossible to know what the talent range is for ANY of your prospects, even if they're past the percentage requirement. Now that sounds like a bug that would've been fixed rather quickly, right? NOPE, EA has not been fazed by a largely talked about bug like that has existed since the release 10 months ago. With a bug that negatively impacts your experience with that capacity, most companies would have something like that patched within a week or slightly more, but EA would rather never touch it, throwing standards WAY out the window. Another very common one is the consistent progress counting errors for the "upgrade and downgrade" system for game abilities. Each ability has their own upgrade and downgrade goal, which if met on the field (like for example "reach 100 rushing yards in a game to upgrade, or "get held to only 75 rushing yards to downgrade) should upgrade/downgrade accordingly. Instead it's more of a gamble for A LOT of the abilities. Many of them will have cases like: needing 100 yards rushing to upgrade, the result of the game is my team rushing for 125, yet it downgrades, acting like you for some reason instead got held something below 75 or something. Other times, the ability will literally count the wrong stat. Had cases where the requirement was "don't allow more than 2 sacks in a game", which my blockers would allow zero sacks, yet it downgraded me because for some reason it will decide to count YOUR DEFENSES sacks to that number, causing you to downgrade because your own defense got sacks. So in short, the systems that are supposed to be unique, and add a interesting touch to the game, will a lot of times do quite the opposite, and just ruin the moment, way too often. Lastly, which is the least inconvenient ones is the display glitches that have never gone away, once again showing the lack of determination to make the game at the very least seem like it's cared for. You'll have the stats that show up for players describing the wrong stats, which for instance there is one where it will show you the characters current season stats on the field, but it is labeled as "2024 season stats". There is a glitch where sometimes on the scoreboard, it will show a score of something like "24 to 35" but on the team stats box score, will show "24 to 28", as if it forgot to count one of the touchdowns somehow, which I'm currently assuming is coming from whenever a score is "booth reviewed" after the play, and in return causes a stat counting glitch that will also effect the total stats of your players for their season stats. Which could be terrible for some cases if a player was leading in their position for touchdowns or something. So in short, what will happen is the game will count the scores after booth review confirms the score, but ends up acting like a score that was given for no reason, removing the fact that a player got the yards and touchdown to make it happen. In the coach abilities page, there will be a bunch of visual bugs with the labeling and upgrade/downgrade section of display. Overall, a bunch of visual displays that while can be funny at times, usually just end up loosing immersion towards the game, and/or are just annoying. So yeah, I don't know how EA just releases this **** without feeling an ounce of shame pricing it at $70, while refusing to do even the most BASIC procedures that most companies would do to polish their game. I would not recommend this game AT ALL for the price of $70, and I'm gonna be honest, even when it's at a discount of $20 (which is when I bought the game), still feels a bit of a stretch considering they don't bother having any standards for the game. These games would genuinely be at the very least decent to nowadays standards, if they would just polish their game, and the systems that are supposed to ENHANCE the game, not making it more frustrating. Buy the game at $20 if you haven't had a football game in a while, and it will probably suffice, for that football game craving. By no means should you be buying this game at $70 though, it's pretty much forcefully scamming yourself.

Another year, another full-price update that feels like a bug-riddled beta. As a long-time fan of the franchise, Football Manager 2026 is a massive disappointment. Instead of delivering meaningful innovation, Sports Interactive has released a product hampered by persistent UI glitches, match engine oddities, and long-standing bugs that have gone unaddressed for multiple patch cycles. The main issues: UI Clutter & Overlapping Text: The interface feels messy and poorly tested. Text scaling is broken across several menus, causing data, stats, and squad depth roles to overlap awkwardly—making simple squad navigation frustrating. Match Engine Anomalies: Defending AI remains deeply flawed. Center-backs still freeze or make bizarre positioning decisions during basic opposition through-balls, while wingers continue shooting into the side netting from impossible angles instead of squaring for an easy tap-in. Tactics & Squad Depth Glitches: Changing formations on tactical tiles frequently fails to update across related screens, requiring manual menu-refreshing to display accurate player positioning. Broken Transfer Logic: AI clubs make illogical transfer bids, and mandatory buy-out clauses or loan agreements still trigger bugged upfront payment demands or disappear outright mid-negotiation. Lack of Real Innovation: Beyond minor visual tweaks, the core gameplay loop feels identical to previous titles—except now you're paying full price to quality-test a release that relies on future patches to become playable. Unless SI rolls out a major overhaul patch, save your money and stick to an older, fully patched edition. Verdict: 4/10 — Feels unfinished and unacceptable even after almost a year

I really wanted to give this game the best possible chance to leave a good impression. I didn’t care that it was buggy. I just wanted to experience another FM game, and I feel like I gave it a very fair shake. I have over 1,000 hours in this game, and I can pretty comfortably say that you are better off playing FM24. This game has a myriad of issues, with the biggest one, in my opinion, being that it feels like you can’t really get much out of the game from a statistics standpoint. Part of that is because the statistics they give you are just all over the place. There’s no real structure to the UI or where things are placed, so you’re constantly digging around trying to find information. And I understand that it’s a new UI and it’s going to take some time to learn it. FM24 took some time to get used to as well, but once you got used to that UI, it was very simple to move around and find what you needed. This UI is just a pain. To this day, I am not entirely sure where certain things are. Wages are a good example. You would think that if you went under wages, you would be able to see how much each player is getting paid. Instead, you get this massive breakdown of your overall wage structure. That does you some good if that’s the information you’re looking for, but most of the time, if I’m going under wages, I want to see how much my players are actually making. I want to see, “Hey, this player is making this much per week.” I don’t need a giant screen full of numbers every time I want that information. The game just feels like it’s taking a massive step backwards. It’s not really enjoyable, and the variance the game displays is insane. You can have one match where your defense is just getting carved up. Okay, you adjust for that and make the changes. Then you have another match where the opponent’s keeper is suddenly looking like prime Petr Čech and cannot be scored on, even though he’s a bad League One goalkeeper. Then you have matches where you’re just getting FM’d and there’s really nothing you can do about it. The opponent has an xG of 0.27 and scores relatively easily, while you can’t finish anything. You look at everything and it seems fine, and there’s no real explanation other than the ball apparently just had to go into the goal. Again, I really wanted to like this game. I wanted to give it every bit of runway I could, and I did. I played multiple saves. I went deep into saves. And when you go deep into saves, you start noticing even more issues, especially with newgens. Finding a good newgen center back is like pulling teeth. I bought the best goalkeeper in the world at one point and still had situations where he was playing the ball around the midfield line for reasons I still do not understand. This game just does not feel like FM24. In FM24, it felt like the game rewarded you for building a good tactic and having elite players. Would you occasionally lose a game? Of course. That’s football. But it also felt like if you wanted to build a team that could go invincible, you absolutely could. You could build a side that was good enough to not lose a match in basically any league in the world. In FM26, that feels more like a pipe dream than anything. It feels like the game is programmed for you to eventually have these losses and punish you no matter how good your tactic is. There is always going to be something the AI finds to exploit in some way, shape, or form. Maybe your keeper does something ridiculous. Maybe their keeper saves everything. Maybe they score from basically nothing. Maybe your defense suddenly forgets how to defend. At some point, something is going to happen that just makes you sit there and wonder what exactly you were supposed to do about it. So this has been a lot of rambling to basically say that I cannot recommend this game. If you want to play Football Manager, play FM24. It’s a far better product, it’s far more customizable, and it’s a lot less frustrating.

I've played this game religiously for 20+ years, spending money every year for what was often just an updated database. That was fine, as the game itself was exactly what it should have been. Often times they'd clearly spend the year making up some shiny new feature, which was usually a nice little addition, but didn't revolutionise the gameplay loop - and that was great, small iterative progress without breaking the core game which worked so well for so many, ideal. And basically free money for SI every year when we forked out another £40 for a database update. I was excited to see them trying something new with this one, naively thinking they'd surely not throw away such an easy business model right? And wow, that launch was something else. The game was so comprehensively broken in every which way it's barely worth talking about. What they had been doing all that time I don't know, as they'd clearly thrown a bunch of the old game into a preset layout already used by other games. Lazy, and just so, so stupid. So I refunded and continued to play fm24, which was a bit stale but basically fine, thinking I'd give it another go in a few months. Here I am, the game is discounted heavily and I have a free evening, so gave it a go. Despite having clearly improved lots of stuff, and the community skins being a big improvement - these fixes are all being slapped onto a house built on sand. The new UI is just so fundamentally poor, that all the iterative improvements in the world will not fix it. It's a nightmare to use, and actually gives me a headache trying to sort through the haphazardly displayed information and endless popups within popups. The match engine is improved, and the graphics slightly too, which is a great little change. Had they just done that and kept the old UI, that would have been golden. But of course they'll have to stick with this popup nonsense now, having put so much on the line to make this ridiculous change. It's a real shame, and hopefully someone pops up to create a competitor finally who can push this company to finally pull their finger out and do the simple things.

I really enjoy FM26, but the current bug reporting process is frustrating. I found what appears to be a reproducible bug with a new stadium project. My Nottingham Forest stadium project had been in progress since 03/06/2030. When it reached its expected completion date, the Board screen showed: * 26/06/2033: **In Progress – 1 day remaining** * 27/06/2033: Still **In Progress**, but the “Completed” field suddenly showed **03/06/2030**, which is actually the original start date * 28/06/2033: Still **In Progress**, now showing **12 months remaining** There was no inbox message, board notification, or explanation for a one-year extension. I also tested this using an older backup save and reproduced exactly the same sequence, so this is not caused by something I did later in the save. I have screenshots from all three dates and a save file from before the issue occurs, so I wanted to report it properly to Sports Interactive. I registered for the Sports Interactive forum, but my account has been stuck on **“Awaiting Approval”**, saying that an email will be sent when the account is approved. So I currently have a reproducible bug, screenshots, a save file, and clear reproduction steps — but no way to submit them through the official bug tracker. Bugs are understandable in a game this complex. What is much harder to accept is making it difficult for players who actually take the time to reproduce and document a bug to report it.

I've played Football Manager for thousands of hours, and this is now the second Football Manager in a row that I can't recommend. The match engine is better. I'll give them that. But almost everything around it feels like a downgrade. International management is easily the biggest disappointment. Sports Interactive spent two years rebuilding it, yet it somehow ended up with less content than before. There's barely anything to do between international breaks, it still feels like an afterthought, and to make things even worse, they removed youth national teams altogether. In the previous game you could manage U21s, U19s and other youth sides. Now you can't. How do you spend two years rebuilding a feature just to remove content? The biggest frustration in my save came after qualifying my home-nation Estonia for its first-ever World Cup. My star centre-back, one of the most important players in my squad, couldn't be registered because he was injured for one day. Not one week. Not one month. One day. On top of that, the game wouldn't even let me register enough players to meet the minimum squad size. Instead of enjoying the biggest achievement of the save, I was fighting against the game's own registration system. That's not realism, it's just poor design. The new UI is another disaster. It may look cleaner, but it's far less practical. Finding simple things has become a chore. Club legends, icons, favoured personnel... why are they so difficult to find now? Half the time I'm just clicking through menus trying to find information that used to be easy to access in the previous game. A prettier interface means nothing if it's slower and harder to use. Then there are the bugs. Instant Result sometimes freezes the entire game, leaving the UI completely unresponsive. You can't click anything, and you can't even close the game normally because the exit confirmation appears but your mouse no longer works. The only way out is opening Task Manager and force closing Football Manager. I've also had random crashes just from pressing the wrong button. One time I clicked "Suggested Squad" on an email, which should've taken me straight to the next email. Instead, the game stayed on the exact same email while the buttons underneath suddenly changed to the ones from the next email. It was like two different emails had merged together. Stuff like this makes the game feel poorly tested. The match engine itself is definitely an improvement, but FM still has far too many matches that make you question what's going on. I'm not saying the game is literally scripted, but it still feels that way far too often. You dominate possession, shots, xG and clear-cut chances, your players suddenly forget how to complete five-yard passes, you hit the woodwork three times, miss open goals, then lose to the opponent's only shot on target. Everyone who's played Football Manager long enough knows exactly the kind of match I'm talking about. That's what makes this so frustrating. The football itself has improved, but almost everything surrounding it has either stagnated or gone backwards. International management is shallower than ever, youth national teams have been removed, the UI is significantly worse, frustrating registration issues still exist, and the game is still plagued by bugs that simply shouldn't be there in a full release. I was already disappointed with the previous Football Manager, so I genuinely hoped this one would get the series back on track. Instead, we got a better match engine wrapped in a worse UI, weaker international management, removed features, frustrating bugs and questionable design choices. Football Manager is still the only game that offers this experience, and that's probably the only reason Sports Interactive keeps getting away with releases like this. If there was real competition, they'd have to do much better. Right now it feels like they're relying on having no competition instead of delivering the quality this series used to be known for. The match engine deserves praise, but one improvement isn't enough when so many other parts of the game have gone backwards. This is the second Football Manager in a row that I can't recommend, and that's something I never thought I'd say.

I was really excited to give this game a try. I was looking forward to creating my own team from scratch, way down in the English national league (below EFL2), and building up this ragtag band of nobodies to superstardom. Instead, after just 45 minutes, I'm doing something I almost NEVER do on Steam: I'm asking for a full refund. I got into the game before realizing you can't create a club on your own. But they have PAID DLC (for actual money) that lets you customize stuff. And now, I'm not even sure if I needed it to begin with, as you actually need to use some "pre-game editor", and I'm not even sure if that's included in the base game or what I paid for. Who cares, right? So, I go through all of this technical nonsense just to find and install and run the editor, and ... drumroll please ... Bupkis. You edit the team, you put in all of this effort, and then you go back to start a new career, and it doesn't show up anywhere in the game. I'm not sure how many times I've ever actually requested refunds on games, but it's rare. I literally own games I played for 7 minutes and never touched again, and I don't ask for a refund because hey, you win some and you lose some. I bought the game. It was my decision. If it stinks, hey, whatever, it stinks. But this is a game I couldn't even start to play, because you jump through all of these hoops just to realize you can't create a new team from scratch. If it's done in an actual, modern, intuitive way that doesn't involve doomscrolling through folders or opening a decrepit ancient game file editor straight out of 1997. Not recommended - even at 50% off I bought FM26 around nine months after release at a 50% discount. This review is based on roughly 25 hours of play and one full season. For context, I used to buy Football Manager roughly every two years, but I had not played or bought one since FM21 in 2022. I was expecting some adjustment after a few years away, but FM26 feels less like a modernised version of the game and more like a frustrating redesign that gets in the way of things I used to enjoy. TL;DR: I would not recommend buying this unless you really cannot wait. At the very least, wait until the end of August for a deeper sale. The biggest issue is the UI. I know this has been widely discussed, but it really does affect the experience. Setting up training feels awkward and unintuitive, and it feels like a significant step backwards from the last version I played. Keeping track of player development and adjusting training used to be one of the parts of FM that kept me invested. In FM26, I have very little desire to engage with it. This also affects youth development. I could not clearly tell what tactics my youth team were using, or how to make sure they were aligned with the first team. Youth training also seems to have been removed or hidden in a way I could not figure out. To be clear, some of these things may be possible and I may simply not have found them, but that is part of the problem. If basic squad development systems are so unintuitive that a returning player cannot work them out after a full season, the design has failed. Cup draws are another strange downgrade. I often skipped through the full draw presentation in older games, but it at least made it obvious that something important was happening. Now it is effectively just another email, and like most emails in real life, I barely notice it. The result is that I often just move from match to match without really feeling aware of what competition I am playing in. There are also various UI bugs and annoyances. In press conferences, I have had questions appear behind the reporter cards, making them impossible to read. The “manager beef” emails are another example of poor interface design: the email summary box often is not large enough to show what was actually said, so you have to click into the article card just to see the relevant comment. That is a common theme across the game: too many clicks to do things that used to feel much quicker. There are smaller frustrations too. When a match is loading, the league table appears, but the two teams playing are not highlighted. By the time I have found both teams, the screen is usually gone. I also have replay settings enabled for disallowed offside goals, but I have not seen a single replay of one I have also had the match engine get stuck in a loop, repeatedly replaying the same minute of a match again and again. The in-game editor is now £7.49, compared with £3.99 for FM21. I have not bought it for FM26, so I cannot comment on whether it has changed meaningfully, but as a returning player that price rise feels unreasonable. There are positives. Loading and processing times feel snappier to me, although I have no hard evidence for that. But faster processing does not make up for the game being less enjoyable to navigate and less satisfying to manage. A common defence seems to be that the UI has been made more console-friendly. I am not convinced. Plenty of views and screens do not even fit properly on my PC monitor, so I do not think “designed for console” explains it. To me, it just feels poorly designed and poorly quality-controlled. It seems like they have made every player fit the "average" development path, rather than having variance among outcomes create that average. It doesn't matter if it's realistic or not though, because it's not fun. Online leagues with human GMs rely on dependable development of prospects. You need this for people to trade. Without trading, online leagues are mostly pointless. In the past 2 versions, no one wants to trade because most prospects fail, and on the other end there are hardly any players worth trading for, because everyone's peak only lasts 2 or 3 years. Winning and losing is no longer based on GM talent, but rather on which GM get's lucky enough to have most of their prospects develop. Almost no one will, but that one person will be golden for 4 to 5 seasons. Hooray. I will continue to purchase as there is no alternative and I do not want to lose my online league friends, but if there was anything else we'd switch immediately. I may still quit. After the last few versions, I told myself OOTP26 was a make or break version for me. Looks like the answer is break.

This is the most ridiculous version I’ve ever played. As an online quick play player, setting up a proper pick-and-roll in this version is virtually impossible. If you stand there waiting for the screen like in previous years, you’ll easily get stripped brainlessly at least ten times a game. You’re forced to develop a mid-range game, which heavily tests your mastery of the shot meter—rewarding rhythm and timing over actual basketball IQ. In the past, beating casuals was simple: as long as you executed solid pick-and-rolls to force mismatches and set up your defense, you’d crush opponents who took bad shots and jacked up random threes. Even if your shot timing wasn’t as green as theirs, your higher basketball IQ allowed you to easily suppress purely mechanical players. However, this year's overpowered on-ball steal mechanic punishes drop coverage severely, costing you tons of possessions. If you manually control the primary ball-handler, you can't drop back effectively to protect the rim, which lowers the barrier for low-IQ players to attack the paint. If your offense is terrible, you can just find a cheese play that exploits the AI defense and run it from the first minute to the last. No adaptability required—just spam the exact same setup and turn the game into a contest of who handles the controller better, strips more balls, and hits more green releases. This version is purely about mechanical skill, making it the least basketball-oriented iteration yet. It’s a total dream for MyCareer players. Drop defense has been heavily nerfed because, as long as the player’s stick skills are good enough, anyone can hit threes—even players who can't shoot to save their life in the actual NBA. To protect players with zero tactical mind, pushing the ball in transition and passing have become the hardest parts of the game. Rewarding mechanical skill is fine, but this turns a rare basketball simulation into just another Esports button-masher.

Madden NFL 26 on PC is borderline unplayable, especially when trying to play online with crossplay enabled. I’m not running this on some outdated setup either — I have an i9-14th Gen CPU, RTX 4070, and 32GB of RAM, and the game still suffers from insane input delay. I’m talking up to 10–20 seconds between pressing a button on my controller and the action happening on screen. In an online football game where timing matters for literally everything, that makes the game impossible to play competitively or even casually enjoy. Menus stutter, gameplay feels delayed, and crossplay somehow makes the experience even worse. It’s ridiculous that a AAA sports title released in 2026 performs this badly on high-end hardware. I pretty much only play Madden for MUT. I enjoy earning card packs and opening them to try to build *my* Ultimate Team. Sadly, EA has made this feature so complicated and convoluted (and done everything they can to force you to pay money), it's basically ruined the whole process. Gone are the days when you could go into Legend Challenges, find the players you idolized as a kid, earn their cards and then spend time playing the game to make those cards better. Now to get the cards you want, you have to have scores of other cards combined into different cards to combine into different cards, then combine those into *different* cards, but along the entire process, you either need to get *extremely* lucky or pay *loads* of cash to have slightly better odds to get the cards you need. The entire goal is, "let's do everything we can to force people into paying to buy as many packs as we can" when it should be, "let's do everything we can to make a fun game". Of course, that's EA's gameplan with everything, so I shouldn't be surprised. The game sure is pretty, but combine the facts above with how unnecessarily complicated and unintuitive the interfaces and menus are; the ridiculous amounts of splash screens, animations, and celebrations you can't cancel out of; the toxic community you're almost *forced* to play with; and the lack of anything new or innovative in years, the only way I can recommend buying the game is on deep discount.

I took a Friday and Saturday off work. Thought, you know what I have enjoyed every other entry from Sports Interactive from Championship Manager in the 90s to Football Manager 2024. I have now played FM26 for 20+ hours and I cannot recommend this game. Positives first, match day, massive upgrade. Yes the graphics aren't on par with EA's offerings, but its a huge leap in terms of animation quality and generally feeling like an actual football match. The tactics are heading in the right direction, not there yet, but in possession and out of possession is definitely the way forward, although the UI can make navigating this annoying. Negatives, the overall presentation is a cluttered mess. It looks like a free to play mobile game. Text is too large even on the smallest text setting. Doesn't appear to be any forethought to placement of cells/boxes. Every thing is so damn hard to find, not in a learning a UI way, more in a why the hell have you put it there way. Had to google how to find my clubs favoured personnel and rival clubs. Because the UI is such a mess it destroys all immersion from the game, I never felt any connection to my own team or the game world as a whole, I felt driven to the next match day with training, staffing, transfers as after thoughts. I only found the game playable using either the CTRL or Material skin, I shouldn't have to rely on the community to make the game playable, I know we have all used skins on previous entries but the base games were perfectly playable without. Its not for me, I am back on FM24. I think maybe if they polish the UI and allow proper skin and custom options then maybe FM27 will work. I am not holding my breath though.

Yellow cards were shown at the world cup, totally unrealistic. More seriously: The UI/UX is garbage. It's awful. Whoever designed it should reconsider their line of work, it is so much harder to find and navigate to whatever menu or display you're looking for. Hell, even just clicking a player or team name takes longer - if you see a top player making a fuss and think "I'll make an offer", you have to open the article, then click the name, rather than just being able to click the name directly as before. It's a minor thing but it's very consistently irritating; everything takes two or three clicks more to find. More positively: the match engine genuinely seems better than the previous iterations of FM for both your and opposition AI, with the exception of wide players. There still seems to be a fundamental problem with various flavours of wingers where they will bomb to the byline - whether they stay wide or cut inside - then they'll drag it back, faff, and more often than not lose possession, or pass to someone who is now marked; rather than square or cut the ball back to unmarked players, regardless of instruction set. I don't think I've seen wing play consistently work since FM12, and even then to a broken level, where overloading with IFs was meta. The engine also still seems to not know how to handle CMs, they seem to trend consistently lower match performance scoring than other roles regardless of their stats, without goals or assists - linking up play doesn't seem to count. Other than that, defensive AI seems much better - marks and intercepts more smartly. I have actually enjoyed the matchday experience in FM26 the most in a long time. Subjectively, I wish that potential ability was more dynamic. While it's too easy to "game" in FIFA/EAFC, this is one area that it is far better in - you can both have and find a Vardy-style player who has developed as a team moves up the leagues; in FM, pretty much everyone has a hard ceiling with the way that Potential Ability works. There is some dynamism (if it works like 24 and earlier), but that's more of an RNG that is rolled on game start. I'd rather see a %age likelihood for it to increase with consistent, multiple seasons of good performances to recognise natural growth or even Drogba-style late bloomers, which don't really exist in FM. Conversely it's very easy to have a high PA not hit their ceiling. I think if they go back to an FM24 style UI, and put some effort into fixing persistent wing play AI, the next iteration might be the first FM that I pick up at launch in almost 15 years. They've gone from "buy every year" starting with Champ Man 98, to "get on discount towards the end of the season" for me. At least they're now trying to revamp.

I absolutely hate the new user interface in Football Manager 26. What used to feel intuitive and efficient now feels like a constant struggle of navigating back and forth through menus, with far too many unnecessary clicks just to get to where you want to be. The whole interface feels like it has been designed around a different type of player. It honestly seems like the developers have made major changes to accommodate console players, and somewhere along the way they have forgotten about the game's core audience: long-time PC players who value depth, efficiency and control. Football Manager has always been about managing a huge amount of information quickly and efficiently. The new UI gets in the way of that. Instead of making the experience smoother, it adds friction to almost every part of the game. It feels like a classic case of fixing something that wasn't broken, and in the process, making the overall experience significantly worse for the people who have been playing and supporting Football Manager for years. Very disappointing. The new UI is, in my opinion, a massive step backwards.

This game is a giant satchel of richards. its like being in a casino where you are made to believe your choices matter, stats matter, and intelligence matters. But the House is always stacked against you no matter what and when it wants you to lose, you will lose. This game can swiftly die off into the abyss and its AI can sink with it as we prep for FM27 in hopes it too will not be another satchel of richards. 1. If the match engine values a tiny handful of physical attributes over everything else, and if the calculation penalties override tactical familiarity and squad quality, then the core gameplay loop loses all meaning. Aka Stats do and don't matter. The Unity Engine is obnoxiously over tuned. It is incredibly frustrating to take every precaution—maintaining high tactical familiarity, building a stacked squad, and avoiding constant changes—only to watch the game repeatedly enforce a "failure cycle." 2. Are Technical Stats Actually Irrelevant? In the current state of FM26, they practically are when compared to physicals. Statistical tests run by the community across thousands of simulated matches consistently prove that Pace, Acceleration, and Strength carry massively disproportionate weight in the match engine's calculations. • A winger with 18 Pace and 10 Dribbling will consistently outperform a winger with 12 Pace and 18 Dribbling. • Because the engine determines that the faster player wins the physical duel check, the high technical attributes of your slower, smarter players never even get activated in the code. This completely breaks the immersion of building a technically brilliant squad and reduces the game to a track-and-field simulator. 3. The Trap of "Over tuned Penalties" The hidden morale and momentum modifiers. • When your team falls into a losing streak, the engine applies massive hidden penalties to your players' hidden attributes (like Confidence and Pressure). • Once these penalties are active, the calculations for success rates (passes completed, tackles won, shots on target) drop drastically. This creates a doom loop. If you stay with your familiar tactic, the negative morale penalties cause you to lose. If you change your tactic, the tactical familiarity penalty causes you to lose. When the engine locks you into a corner where every single mathematical avenue leads to a 3-goal loss, the game stops being a management simulator and becomes a frustrating, rigged calculator. That is all. If FM27 has the same engine but a different shiny new UI which everyone and their mother were ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ about, then nothing actually changes, congrats you still have lipstick on a pig. GLHF

Caveat: I do not play offline. I play Perfect Team only. This game is a complete mess. The bugs are extensive. You cannot view splits data in tournaments. You cannot view splits data for previous seasons in league play. In league play, there is normalization, which causes a lot more randomness to occur throughout the season. The community managers are great, and the discord community is great. The game is pretty abysmal. It is great fun to collect your favorite players and build lineups and live the "Dream-Team" dream. But it is immensely frustrating to put all of this work in week after week and just lose to RNG in the playoffs, week after week. (I am in fact writing this review in frustration, as my team went 99-63 in the regular season for the top seed, then lost in the first round to a team that went 80-82.) This has been a weekly occurrence for me in Perfect Team. I haven't made it out of the LCS round of the playoffs since the first month of the game's release, but my team has been above 90 wins EVERY SINGLE WEEK. If you are prone to frustration at RNG, I really cannot recommend this game, and that's where I land. My time spent and work that I've put in (I have 3 different PowerBI Dashboards for this game specifically) feel meaningless at the end of the day. If you don't care and just want to play a baseball game that isn't The Show or SMB, that requires very little skill and only baseball knowledge, AND you like TCGs, then this game is probably going to be fun for you. But there are also bugs and annoying quirks. It could be so much better, considering the microtransactions are certainly creating piles of money for them. This game DOES have whales, and I don't care about that, but I know some do, and they are absolutely ALL OVER this game. And knowing that it will all go POOF when the next game comes out in March is incredibly frustrating. After 3000 hours spent, I can confidently say: stay away from OOTP.

2k26 is genuinely a good game if you are going for a semi-realistic NBA simulation. The controls may feel delayed/unresponsive but that sometimes just depends on your PC and the animations itself. Some animations feel REALLY responsive and some do not. As you can see, I have nearly 1k hours of gameplay in 2k26 and that is because I genuinely enjoy it, but despite all that, I will never give this game a good rating. Before you purchase the game, be ready for A LOT of FRUSTRATING bugs and issues. 1. Some people say the jump shot is too easy at times, and this may be true. I can go on a whole 48-minute MyCareer game barely missing from the 3 point line (40+ 3s a game and 10 misses at MOST), however the reason why I have an issue with the shooting mechanics is because the game SOMETIMES will be severely delayed (again this might just be because of my PC) causing you to miss the shot or the game will simply change up the rhythm of the shooting even if there's no one contesting you. Though the Devs have confirmed that the shooting does not rely entirely on RNG, the mere fact that it exists will inevitably F up your gameplay. 2. This is mainly the reason why I gave this game a bad review. For the NBA fans out there, besides the fans that just enjoy 2k26 as a game, you know how the referees in modern NBA can be REALLY CHEESY especially when its in favor of OKC, well guess what, 2k26 may or may not have intentionally incorporated it into the game, BUT ITS THERE AND ITS F***ING ANNOYING. The salt to the wound that honestly caused me to create this review is THE INCONSISTENCY OF THESE AWFUL CALLS. Sometimes, the refs are not bugging, but sometimes, you will get your 5th foul off of bulls**t calls (sometimes the animation causes you to foul like a blocking foul wherein the player cuts off the offensive player and gets charged but instead of a charging foul you get a defensive blocking foul). One of the MyCareer saves that I have on 2k26 averages 7.7 blocks a game (non-simulated is actually 10 blocks per game I try to average a quadruple double) so this means I often go for every single jumpshot, and there are times where I get 15+ blocks in a game without barely getting fouls, but then 2k26 in some games will have SEVERELY CHEESY REFS. I am not exaggerating when I say that these MFing REFS are straight hell spawns. They will literally call clean blocks fouls, and when you challenge the call, the call still stands. It is SUPER outrageous how cheesy some of these calls can get. I once challenged a call wherein my center didn't even make body contact with the person who drew the foul, literally no body contact, and the call still stood. One of the most common awful calls I noticed is 2k26 calling a body contact after the clean block a foul. I know that in the NBA, it sometimes is a foul if youre in the shooters landing space even after the shot is already thrown or if you hit the player after the shot, but in 2k, even if the natural motion of both players inevitably creates contact even after a clean block, 2k26 cancels the block and gives you a foul. Mind you, they will initially count the blocks but if your players hand touches the opponents hands after, its a foul, even if there was no other way to block the shot. You can't tell me that it simply is just a foul because sometimes, 2k26 will not call it. The inconsistency is VERY infuriating. The calls in this game is genuinely broken and not in a way that will favor the player, so please for the love of GOD, if you are thinking of buying this game regardless if it's on sale or not, just DO NOT. 2k is already a multimillion dollar company and they can't even fix simple issues such as mentioned. Do not give them your hard earned money.

This game is sadly abysmal. (I played the MyCareer only, that was more than enough for me.) About 10-15 years ago I loved the NBA2K titles for their MyCareer, they were better than most RPG-s. Though 26 still has it, the bad things make it meaningless. I understand that there had to be some factors chosen, how should MP-s story fold out but punishing the player after winning a match just because you didn't win DOMINANT ENOUGH is a no for me. I win, I was glad with the performance and game says, sorry kid, you were supposed to be the next GOAT, so want to retry or want to quit? I quit for good. The characters I've met in the short-lived journey were OK, I liked MP's bonding with his parents. The atmosphere is overwhelming for a newcomer. I'm not used to wait enormous times when playing a game. Keep in mind that my playtime is mostly waiting, I had to wait for an entire hour after the first start so the game built some shaders. Don't relax, it would do it every time, well, not an hour long, just a minute for the other times, but it is still a big no. Wherever I go in the game, because MyCareer feels like some kind om MMO now if you are in the city is the same, wait for the shader buildup, usually 5-10 minutes. (Never again.) At first start, you don't get into the main menu, the game pushes you right into MyCareer. OK, I would have chosen that but forcing is bad, I always like to get to settings first. First forced game, doesn't even know what button should I press, but the game forces you to play. Still managed to beat the opposition with only passing figured out. Later I could finally get into the settings but not for much good. Maybe I was sidetracked, but I didn't see a tab for visuals, resolution, etc, so I don't know what default was, but visuals were ugly and the game still wasn't smooth. The MMO gives 2012 Need for Speed Most Wanted vibes, totally alien, unreal, artificial and needless. The music is good, the sounds, the character voices are the upside. But they can't do magic. I got to give credit to the devs, they made something unique. The conception is good, the delivery is not. If you are a hardcore fan, have a decent controller and very good machine, you might have a good enough experience, but I can't recommend this title even on a sale. If you want premium basketball, buy a previous title.

Game might not be bad, idk because I can't figure out how to do ♥♥♥♥ on KB/M. It's completely fine for a game to suggest the use of a controller, but to have such little support for KB/M is heinous. This has to be a lazy console port or something. The tutorial doesn't even explain how to play/what the binds are on KB/M, and in fact, the whole game always assumes that you are exclusively using controller. This is a problem that's making it very hard for me to learn how to play. And yeah, some people will automatically jump to "just get a controller lol" but that's not the point. If I don't have a controller plugged in, it shouldn't be telling me to press a certain controller button to do a certain thing. It should tell me how to do it on KB/M. There's also times where you are forced to press a button on your keyboard instead of just clicking the button that's on the screen with your mouse. I was gonna say that the game looks bad as well, but I found out that the game was running in 1280x720 for whatever reason, and the game looks much better now that I've fixed it. If the game looks god-awful on install for you too, this is probably why. But yeah, it's an NBA 2K game. Didn't expect much out of it, and I was right to hold that opinion.
